TITLE: ТОЧНО ИЗЧИСЛЯВАНЕ НА КРАЙНИЯ ПРОФИЛ НА ДОПУСТИМИТЕ АМАЛГАМАЦИИ

STATUS:
FINITE JOINTLY-GENERATED PROFILE ENUMERATED
TWO STRONG AMALGAMATION CLASSES IDENTIFIED
THREE TOTAL ADMISSIBLE CORE CLASSES IDENTIFIED
CARRIER IDENTIFICATION DISTINGUISHED FROM NON-APARTNESS
MINIMAL RELATION SHOWN NOT TO ENCODE STRONGNESS BY ITSELF
NO CANONICAL R CLAIM
NO FROZEN CORE CHANGE

============================================================
1. INPUT SPAN
============================================================

S0={a,b}
S1={a,b,c}
S2={a,b,d}

Each source carries standard inequality apartness:
x #i y iff x != y.

The span maps are the inclusions:
i1:S0->S1
i2:S0->S2.

An admissible amalgamation consists of embeddings:
j1:S1->A
j2:S2->A
such that:
j1 o i1 = j2 o i2.

For this finite enumeration, use the auxiliary apartness axioms:
1. irreflexivity;
2. symmetry;
3. cotransitivity:
   x#y => (x#z or z#y), for every z.

The source embeddings must preserve and reflect the apartness relation on their own source carriers.

============================================================
2. JOINTLY-GENERATED CARRIER CONVENTION
============================================================

To obtain a finite profile, restrict first to amalgams whose carrier is generated by the images of S1 and S2:
A = j1(S1) union j2(S2).

This excludes arbitrary additional elements unrelated to the span.

Isomorphisms are required to commute with the fixed source maps j1 and j2. Thus source-labelled points cannot be permuted independently of the diagram.

Without the jointly-generated restriction, arbitrary extra carrier elements produce further extensions and the profile is not the finite three-class set computed below.

============================================================
3. FORCED APARTNESS PAIRS
============================================================

The embedding conditions force:
j1(a)#j1(b)
j1(a)#j1(c)
j1(b)#j1(c)
j2(a)#j2(b)
j2(a)#j2(d)
j2(b)#j2(d).

After identifying the common base, write the images as a,b,c,d where applicable.

The only cross-source pair whose apartness truth value is not fixed by the source restrictions is the pair represented by c,d.

The embeddings also force:
a != b
a != c
b != c
a != d
b != d.

There are two logically distinct questions:
A. Are the images of c and d the same carrier element?
B. If they are distinct, are they apart?

Non-apartness does not imply equality.

============================================================
4. STRONG AMALGAMATION PROFILE
============================================================

Strongness requires:
j1(S1) intersect j2(S2) = j1(S0) = j2(S0).

Therefore j1(c) and j2(d) must be distinct.

On the jointly-generated carrier, all forced apartness pairs are fixed and only c#d remains free.

CASE A1: c#d.

The apartness relation is full inequality on {a,b,c,d}.
This is A_STRONG.

CASE A2: not(c#d), with c and d distinct.

The apartness relation is:
a#b, b#a,
a#c, c#a,
b#c, c#b,
a#d, d#a,
b#d, d#b,
and neither c#d nor d#c.

Equivalently, apartness is inequality between the blocks of:
{{a},{b},{c,d}}.

This is A_GENERATED.

Both structures satisfy irreflexivity, symmetry and cotransitivity.
Both source inclusions are exact embeddings.
Both are strong.

There are no other strong relation choices on the jointly-generated carrier because all pairs other than {c,d} are forced.

Therefore:
Profile_strong(D) = {A1,A2}
and:
|Profile_strong(D)| = 2.

============================================================
5. ALL ADMISSIBLE CORE AMALGAMATIONS
============================================================

If strongness is not required, the cross-source images c and d may be identified.

CASE A3: j1(c)=j2(d).

The jointly-generated carrier has three elements {a,b,c}.
Its apartness is full inequality, as required by the source restrictions.
The two source images intersect in {a,b,c}, so the amalgam is not strong.

No other cross-identification is possible:
- c cannot be identified with a or b because j1 is injective;
- d cannot be identified with a or b because j2 is injective;
- a and b are distinct in the common base.

Thus, under the jointly-generated convention, the complete admissible core profile has exactly:
A1: c and d distinct, c#d;
A2: c and d distinct, not(c#d);
A3: c and d identified.

Hence:
Profile_core(D) = {A1,A2,A3}
and:
|Profile_core(D)| = 3.

The isomorphism classes are distinct over the fixed span because:
- A1 and A2 differ in the truth value of c#d;
- A3 has a different carrier identification, namely j1(c)=j2(d).

============================================================
6. COTRANSITIVITY CHECK VIA PARTITIONS
============================================================

For the finite structures in this test, each listed apartness relation is the relation of belonging to different blocks of a partition.

A1 partition:
{{a},{b},{c},{d}}

A2 partition:
{{a},{b},{c,d}}

A3 partition:
{{a},{b},{c}}

For a relation defined by:
x#y iff x and y lie in different partition blocks,
irreflexivity and symmetry hold immediately.
Cotransitivity holds because if x and y lie in different blocks, then for any z, z cannot lie in both of those blocks; hence x#z or z#y.

The source restrictions are exact:
- on S1, the induced partition is {{a},{b},{c}};
- on S2, the induced partition is {{a},{b},{d}}, or {{a},{b},{c}} in the identified A3 representation after applying the source map.

Therefore all three cases satisfy the stated auxiliary apartness axioms and exact source restrictions.

============================================================
7. WHAT THE MINIMAL GENERATED RELATION DOES AND DOES NOT RECORD
============================================================

On the fixed four-element coproduct carrier with c,d kept as distinct carrier points, the least relation containing all source-image apartness pairs is A2:
#gen = all forced source pairs, with not(c#d).

This is the minimal generated positive apartness relation and is the RelFin_hom pushout structure from the prior checkpoint.

However, #gen alone does not encode whether c and d are:
- distinct but not apart (A2); or
- identified as one carrier element (A3).

These are different carrier structures and different amalgamation types.

Thus the full constraint profile must retain both:
1. carrier identification/equality data;
2. apartness relation data.

A relational profile that stores only positive apartness facts is insufficient to distinguish A2 from A3.

The strongness predicate also cannot be inferred from the positive apartness relation alone. It depends on the carrier-image intersection/equality data.

============================================================
8. PROFILE SUMMARY
============================================================

Under the jointly-generated finite-core convention:

Profile_strong(D) = {A1,A2}
Profile_core(D) = {A1,A2,A3}

Counts:
strong admissible classes = 2
all admissible core classes = 3

If arbitrary extra carrier elements are permitted, there are further extensions. Therefore the number three is not a count of every possible ambient extension; it is the exact count of jointly-generated core amalgams over the fixed span.

The source-level compatibility predicate is:
CC_source(D)=1
because Profile_core(D) is nonempty (and also because Profile_strong(D) is nonempty if the selected CC realization requires strong amalgams).

The truth value CC=1 does not select among A1, A2, or A3.

============================================================
9. CONSEQUENCES FOR R_alt
============================================================

A minimally adequate profile representation for this test must retain:
- the carrier identification pattern;
- the apartness relation on the resulting carrier;
- the source embeddings/restriction maps;
- the strong/non-strong status;
- the isomorphism class over the fixed diagram.

A candidate data type is:
R_alt(D) = (CarrierPattern, ApartnessRelation, SourceMaps, Strongness, ProfileClass).

This is a test-level data schema, not a canonical definition of R.

If R_alt stores only #gen on the four-element carrier, it selects A2 as a minimal generated representative but loses the A3 carrier-identification alternative and the A1 additional apartness alternative.

If R_alt stores the full profile, it preserves the three core alternatives but does not select one R realization. A separate source-authorized selection rule or a realization-space interpretation is still required.
